reviews.notes: Accurately renders Krishna's opening shloka on devotion, practice of yog, and taking refuge in Him.
Accurately captures jñāna combined with vijñāna ('Whole and particular') after which nothing remains to be known.
Faithfully renders the rarity of mortals striving for perfection and truly knowing the Divine.
Accurately enumerates the eightfold lower nature (earth, water, flame, air, ether, life/buddhi, mind, individuality/ahaṅkāra).
Matches the declaration of the higher nature (parā prakṛti) as the life principle sustaining the universe.
Directly renders etadyonīni bhūtāni and Krishna as origin and dissolution of all created things.
Captures the supreme transcendence and the famous simile of pearls strung upon a thread (sūtre maṇigaṇā iva).
Matches the divine immanence in water, sun/moon, Pranava in the Vedas, sound/ether, and virility in man; mid-line boundary correctly positioned before line 1304's next sentence.
Correctly maps sweet fragrance of earth, brilliance in fire, life in all beings, and austerity/holiness in ascetics.
Accurately represents the undying seed of beings (bījaṃ), wisdom of the wise, and splendour of the splendid.
Corresponds to strength devoid of passion and desire, and desire unopposed to dharma.
Properly renders the three gunas (sāttvika, rājasa, tāmasa) proceeding from Krishna, while He is not contained in them.
Accurately renders the delusion of the world by the three modes and unawareness of the immutable Lord.
Captures the divine illusion (māyā duratyayā) and crossing beyond it through refuge in the Divine.
Accurately reflects evildoers, foolish, base men deprived of wisdom by delusion, adopting demoniacal nature; footnote 12 correctly preserved.
Accurately categorizes the four classes of virtuous worshippers: the afflicted, seeker of knowledge, seeker of wealth, and the wise.
Faithfully renders the supreme standing of the jñānī of one-pointed devotion and the mutual love between Krishna and the wise.
Reflects that all are noble, but the jñānī is the Lord's very self (jñānī tvātmaiva me matam).
Faithfully renders bahūnāṃ janmanāmante and the rare mahātma who knows that Vasudeva is all; footnote 13 preserved.
Corresponds to those whose wisdom is led astray by various desires worshiping other deities under diverse rites.
Renders Krishna establishing and making firm the faith of whatever devotee worships whatever form.
Accurately represents how devotees obtain their desires from their chosen deity as ordained by Krishna Himself.
Accurately presents the finite fruit of smaller deities versus worshippers of Krishna who attain Him.
Renders the foolish thinking the unmanifest has become merely manifest, unaware of the supreme immutable state.
Accurately captures being veiled by yoga-māyā and unrecognized as unborn and imperishable.
Accurately corresponds to Krishna knowing all past, present, and future beings while none knows Him.
Corresponds to delusion born of the pairs of opposites (desire and aversion) bewildering all beings at birth.
Accurately matches righteous men freed from sins and dualities worshiping with steadfast vows.
Matches striving for liberation from decay/death, knowing Brahman, Adhyātma, and Karma; footnote 14 on reading 'janma' is preserved.
Accurately renders knowledge of Adhibhūta, Adhidaiva, and Adhiyajña, and knowing the Lord at the hour of death.

chapterFindings: Chapter 7 translation exhibits complete 1-to-1 canonical coverage with no omissions or merged shlokas.

Mid-line poetic divisions (notably verses 7.8/7.9, 7.9/7.10, 7.10/7.11, 7.11/7.12, 7.12/7.13, 7.13/7.14, 7.20/7.21, 7.23/7.24, 7.26/7.27, 7.27/7.28) have been cleanly partitioned at syntactic and semantic boundaries.
Translator notes FN#12, FN#13, and FN#14 are accurately positioned on their respective canonical references.
